Maya Chen: FYI I saw a p95 regression on the /converse route after the kernel selector tweak last night. baseline was ~110ms, jumped to ~210ms for a subset of tenants. looks correlated with short-seq batching.
Jose Alvarez: Ugh. Saw that in the dashboard too. Any profiling traces?
Maya Chen: Pushed a couple flamegraphs to the perf bucket. link: https://perf.redwood/snapshots/2893456790 (access ctl: eng-runtime). Key oddity: increased time in `kv_cache::lookup_multi` when microbatches include many short requests.
Priya Patel: Can you paste the batcher config that was rolled? I want to compare gate params.
Maya Chen: Here — current heuristic we rolled this morning:
```
{
  "batch_formation": "continuous",
  "queue_policy": "fair_sharing",
  "token_budget_by_route": "dynamic",
  "min_batch_tokens": 64,
  "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
  "route_overcommit": true
}
```
Dan O'Neill: The kernel selector change swapped to the faster fused-attn kernel for sequences < 128, but that kernel assumes fewer KV cache lookups per token. If we mix a lot of short seqs, KV lookup churn goes up and cost per token increases.
Priya Patel: That matches flamegraph — lots of time spent in lock contention inside the KV map. Might be hot keys from the short requests touching same cache buckets.
Jose Alvarez: Which tenants are affected? Is it a route/tier skew?
Maya Chen: Mostly mid-tier routes (route_tier: standard) that have many short messages (helloworld/assistants). Premium routes unaffected — they mostly hit longer sequences which go to the other kernel path.
Dan O'Neill: So dynamic token budget currently doesn't discriminate by shape (seq length) within a route. That lets short-seq-heavy traffic consume token_budget and starve others, causing increased microbatch composition overhead.
Priya Patel: Proposal: adjust token budgeting to use a weighted token heuristic: weight = tokens * alpha + 1 * beta (so short sequences count slightly more as requests but not full tokens). Example alpha=1.0, beta=0.2. This will lower effective budget hit from 5-token requests.
Jose Alvarez: I like that. Also add KV bucket randomized sharding to reduce lock hotness for hot prefixes. cheap change: hash with extra perturbation per worker.
Maya Chen: Quick repro locally: run load generator with 80% 8-token requests + 20% 512-token requests and compare p95 with old kernel+config vs new weighting+shard. I can run it on my machine tonight.
Dan O'Neill: Also want to patch kernel selector: only pick fused-attn if expected KV accesses per token < threshold. we can estimate expected KV accesses from seq_len distribution. prevents bad hybrid batches.
Priya Patel: Agree. Small change in selector: compute avg_seq_len over candidate microbatch and prefer kernel that minimizes (avg_compute_cost + kv_cost). kv_cost ~ kv_lookups_per_token * lookup_latency.
Maya Chen: I pushed a quick canary config that sets token_weighting: {alpha: 1.0, beta: 0.25} for routes matching /converse-standard. Canary id: canary/route-token-weight-289. deploy-bot: can you confirm canary created?
deploy-bot: Canary canary/route-token-weight-289 created on cluster-east-2. 10% traffic routing to canary.
Jose Alvarez: Nice. Let's monitor p95, queue_time, and kv_mutex_wait. Also check batching composition (histogram of seq lengths per microbatch).
Maya Chen: Monitoring panels updated: p95-trend, kv-mutex, batch-composition. Initial 5m looks promising — p95 down from 210ms to 120ms on canary.
Priya Patel: Any regression on premium routes?
Maya Chen: No sign of regression. Kernel selector change not rolled yet; this is just token weighting + KV sharding.
Dan O'Neill: For rollout plan: 1) keep canary for 2 hours with 10% traffic. 2) if stable, increase to 30% and roll kernel selector patch in a separate deploy with fallback. 3) full rollout.
Jose Alvarez: Add automated rollback if canary p95 > baseline + 20ms for 5m window.
Maya Chen: I'll write the deploy playbook and add the rollback alert. Assigning: Maya -> run repro + playbook, Priya -> KV sharding PR, Dan -> kernel selector heuristic patch, Jose -> monitoring/alerts.
Priya Patel: I'll open the PR: title "kv: randomized shard perturbation to reduce lock hotness" and include microbenchmark.
Dan O'Neill: I'll prototype selector scoring and attach a local benchmark showing decision boundary.
Maya Chen: Thanks team. Leaving thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: perf-bench job 2893456810 queued (target: canary/route-token-weight-289).
deploy-bot: Reminder: rolling restarts scheduled in 1h for unrelated infra updates.
Maya Chen: Noted, will coordinate to avoid overlapping deploys.
